answer: At a harbor beside a willow grove, dispatch agents must reserve scarce loading slots with prepaid, nonrefundable fees. The port signs each slot ID; a contract accepts one claim per ID and binds it to the recipient and service date, blocking replay across wallets. Payment follows an independently signed unloading receipt. A ripple of new identities creates no extra slots, and buying unused slots still costs money. Fees must exceed the gain from a fake delivery. This depends on honest port attestations; a corrupt port can fabricate capacity and defeat it.
